sanskrit: evam uktas tu sugrīvo rāmeṇārtena vānaraḥ abravīt prāñjalir vākyaṃ sabāṣpaṃ bāṣpagadgadaḥ
english: Thus addressed by the grief-stricken Rāma, the monkey Sugrīva spoke with hands folded in reverence, his voice choked with tears and his speech broken by weeping.

sanskrit: na jāne nilayaṃ tasya sarvathā pāparakṣasaḥ sāmarthyaṃ vikramaṃ vāpi dauṣkuleyasya vā kulam
english: "I do not know the abode of that wicked demon in any way, nor his power, his prowess, nor indeed the lineage or family of that base-born one.

sanskrit: satyaṃ tu pratijānāmi tyaja śokam ariṃdama kariṣyāmi tathā yatnaṃ yathā prāpsyasi maithilīm
english: Yet I truly promise you: abandon your grief, O subduer of enemies — I shall make such effort that you will recover the daughter of Mithilā.

sanskrit: rāvaṇaṃ sagaṇaṃ hatvā paritoṣyātmapauruṣam tathāsmi kartā nacirād yathā prīto bhaviṣyasi
english: Having slain Rāvaṇa together with his retinue and having satisfied my own valor, I shall act in such a way that before long you will be pleased.

sanskrit: alaṃ vaiklavyam ālambya dhairyam ātmagataṃ smara tvadvidhānāṃ na sadṛśam īdṛśaṃ buddhilāghavam
english: Enough of clinging to this despondency — recall the inner fortitude natural to you. Such mental feebleness does not befit one of your kind.

sanskrit: mayāpi vyasanaṃ prāptaṃ bhāryā haraṇajaṃ mahat na cāham evaṃ śocāmi na ca dhairyaṃ parityaje
english: I too have suffered a great calamity born of the abduction of my wife, yet I do not grieve in this manner, nor do I abandon my fortitude.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ tām anuśocāmi prākṛto vānaro 'pi san mahātmā ca vinītaś cā kiṃ punar dhṛtimān bhavān
english: I, a mere common monkey, do not mourn her — you who are high-souled and well-disciplined, how much less should you who are so resolute grieve!

sanskrit: bāṣpam āpatitaṃ dhairyān nigrahītuṃ tvam arhasi maryādāṃ sattvayuktānāṃ dhṛtiṃ notsraṣṭum arhasi
english: You ought to restrain these tears that have come upon you through lack of fortitude; you ought not to abandon the steadfastness that is the mark of those endowed with true courage.

sanskrit: vyasane vārtha kṛcchre vā bhaye vā jīvitāntage vimṛśan vai svayā buddhyā dhṛtimān nāvasīdati
english: In calamity, or in hardship, or in fear, even when life itself is at stake — one who reflects with his own reason and remains steadfast does not sink into despair.

sanskrit: bāliśas tu naro nityaṃ vaiklavyaṃ yo 'nuvartate sa majjaty avaśaḥ śoke bhārākrānteva naur jale
english: But the man who perpetually follows after despondency is a fool — helplessly he sinks into grief, like a ship in water overwhelmed by its cargo.

sanskrit: eṣo 'ñjalir mayā baddhaḥ praṇayāt tvāṃ prasādaye pauruṣaṃ śraya śokasya nāntaraṃ dātum arhasi
english: With these hands folded in supplication, I entreat you out of affection: take refuge in your valor — you ought not to give room to grief.

sanskrit: ye śokam anuvartante na teṣāṃ vidyate sukham tejaś ca kṣīyate teṣāṃ na tvaṃ śocitum arhasi
english: Those who follow grief find no happiness, and their energy diminishes. You should not grieve thus.

sanskrit: hitaṃ vayasya bhāvena brūhi nopadiśāmi te vayasyatāṃ pūjayan me na tvaṃ śocitum arhasi
english: I speak to you as your well-wisher, with a friend's regard — I do not presume to instruct you. Honoring our friendship, you should not grieve, I say."

sanskrit: madhuraṃ sāntvitas tena sugrīveṇa sa rāghavaḥ mukham aśrupariklinnaṃ vastrāntena pramārjayat
english: Sweetly consoled by Sugrīva in this manner, that scion of the Raghu clan wiped his face, wet with tears, with the hem of his garment.

sanskrit: prakṛtiṣṭhas tu kākutsthaḥ sugrīvavacanāt prabhuḥ saṃpariṣvajya sugrīvam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Restored to his natural composure by Sugrīva's words, that mighty Kākutstha embraced Sugrīva and spoke these words:

sanskrit: kartavyaṃ yad vayasyena snigdhena ca hitena ca anurūpaṃ ca yuktaṃ ca kṛtaṃ sugrīva tat tvayā
english: "What ought to be done by a friend who is affectionate and well-meaning, what is fitting and proper — all that you have done, Sugrīva.

sanskrit: eṣa ca prakṛtiṣṭho 'ham anunītas tvayā sakhe durlabho hīdṛśo bandhur asmin kāle viśeṣataḥ
english: And indeed I have been restored to my natural state by your entreaties, O friend. Such a kinsman as this is rare to find, especially in a time like this.

sanskrit: kiṃ tu yatnas tvayā kāryo maithilyāḥ parimārgaṇe rākṣasasya ca raudrasya rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ
english: Yet effort must be made by you to search for the daughter of Mithilā, and against that fierce demon, the evil-souled Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: mayā ca yad anuṣṭheyaṃ visrabdhena tad ucyatām varṣāsv iva ca sukṣetre sarvaṃ saṃpadyate tava
english: And let what I must do be told to me in confidence — as rain on good soil, all shall come to fruition for you.

sanskrit: mayā ca yad idaṃ vākyam abhimānāt samīritam tat tvayā hariśārdūla tattvam ity upadhāryatām
english: And this speech uttered by me in pride — let it be taken by you, O tiger among monkeys, as the truth.

sanskrit: anṛtaṃ noktapūrvaṃ me na ca vakṣye kadā cana etat te pratijānāmi satyenaiva śapāmi te
english: I have never spoken a falsehood before, nor shall I ever speak one — this I promise you, and by truth itself I swear to you."

sanskrit: tataḥ prahṛṣṭaḥ sugrīvo vānaraiḥ sacivaiḥ saha rāghavasya vacaḥ śrutvā pratijñātaṃ viśeṣataḥ
english: Then Sugrīva was delighted, along with his monkey ministers, having heard the words of the scion of the Raghu clan — above all, the vow that was made.

sanskrit: mahānubhāvasya vaco niśamya harir narāṇām ṛṣabhasya tasya kṛtaṃ sa mene harivīra mukhyas tadā svakāryaṃ hṛdayena vidvān
english: Having heard the words of that great-spirited one, the bull among men, that foremost hero among monkeys — knowing in his heart that his own purpose was as good as accomplished — considered it done.

sanskrit: parituṣṭas tu sugrīvas tena vākyena vānaraḥ lakṣmaṇasyāgrajaṃ rāmam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Thoroughly pleased by those words, the monkey Sugrīva spoke these words to Rāma, the elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa:

sanskrit: sarvathāham anugrāhyo devatānām asaṃśayaḥ upapannaguṇopetaḥ sakhā yasya bhavān mama
english: "I am, without doubt, blessed by the gods in every way — I, whose friend is you, endowed with qualities both natural and acquired.

sanskrit: śakyaṃ khalu bhaved rāma sahāyena tvayānagha surarājyam api prāptuṃ svarājyaṃ kiṃ punaḥ prabho
english: Truly, O Rāma, O sinless one, with you as ally it would be possible to win even the kingdom of the gods — how much more my own kingdom, O lord?

sanskrit: so 'haṃ sabhājyo bandhūnāṃ suhṛdāṃ caiva rāghava yasyāgnisākṣikaṃ mitraṃ labdhaṃ rāghavavaṃśajam
english: I am to be honored by kinsmen and friends alike, O scion of the Raghu clan, for I have gained as a friend, with fire as witness, one born of the Raghu lineage.

sanskrit: aham apy anurūpas te vayasyo jñāsyase śanaiḥ na tu vaktuṃ samartho 'haṃ svayam ātmagatān guṇān
english: I too am a fitting companion for you — you shall come to know this gradually. Yet I am not capable of proclaiming my own inner qualities myself.

sanskrit: mahātmanāṃ tu bhūyiṣṭhaṃ tvadvidhānāṃ kṛtātmanām niścalā bhavati prītir dhairyam ātmavatām iva
english: For great-souled ones like you, those who have mastered themselves, the affection that arises is steadfast — like the fortitude of those who possess true self-possession.

sanskrit: rajataṃ vā suvarṇaṃ vā vastrāṇy ābharaṇāni vā avibhaktāni sādhūnām avagacchanti sādhavaḥ
english: Silver or gold, garments or ornaments — the good regard these as undivided and held in common: such is the understanding of the good.

sanskrit: āḍhyo vāpi daridro vā duḥkhitaḥ sukhito 'pi vā nirdoṣo vā sadoṣo vā vayasyaḥ paramā gatiḥ
english: Whether wealthy or poor, whether in sorrow or in happiness, whether blameless or at fault — a true companion is the highest refuge.

sanskrit: dhanatyāgaḥ sukhatyāgo dehatyāgo 'pi vā punaḥ vayasyārthe pravartante snehaṃ dṛṣṭvā tathāvidham
english: Giving up wealth, giving up comfort, and even giving up one's body — men act thus for the sake of a friend, when they have seen affection of such a kind.

sanskrit: tat tathety abravīd rāmaḥ sugrīvaṃ priyavādinam lakṣmaṇasyāgrato lakṣmyā vāsavasyeva dhīmataḥ
english: To Sugrīva who spoke such agreeable words, Rāma said "so be it" — in the presence of Lakṣmaṇa, as Indra the wise might reply to his glorious companion.

sanskrit: tato rāmaṃ sthitaṃ dṛṣṭvā lakṣmaṇaṃ ca mahābalam sugrīvaḥ sarvataś cakṣur vane lolam apātayat
english: Then, seeing Rāma standing there and the mighty Lakṣmaṇa beside him, Sugrīva let his gaze wander restlessly in all directions through the forest.

sanskrit: sa dadarśa tataḥ sālam avidūre harīśvaraḥ supuṣpam īṣatpatrāḍhyaṃ bhramarair upaśobhitam
english: Then that lord of monkeys saw, not far away, a śāla tree in full bloom, with somewhat sparse foliage but adorned by humming bees.

sanskrit: tasyaikāṃ parṇabahulāṃ bhaṅktvā śākhāṃ supuṣpitām sālasyāstīrya sugrīvo niṣasāda sarāghavaḥ
english: Breaking off one leafy, well-flowering branch of that śāla tree, Sugrīva spread it out and sat down together with Rāma.

sanskrit: tāv āsīnau tato dṛṣṭvā hanūmān api lakṣmaṇam sālaśākhāṃ samutpāṭya vinītam upaveśayat
english: Then seeing the two seated, Hanūmān too pulled off a śāla branch and had Lakṣmaṇa seated upon it with due courtesy.

sanskrit: tataḥ prahṛṣṭaḥ sugrīvaḥ ślakṣṇaṃ madhurayā girā uvāca praṇayād rāmaṃ harṣavyākulitākṣaram
english: Then the delighted Sugrīva, with smooth and sweet speech, spoke to Rāma out of affection, his words faltering with joy:

sanskrit: ahaṃ vinikṛto bhrātrā carāmy eṣa bhayārditaḥ ṛśyamūkaṃ girivaraṃ hṛtabhāryaḥ suduḥkhitaḥ
english: "I, wronged by my brother, wander here tormented by fear, on the excellent mountain Ṛśyamūka, my wife stolen away, in great misery.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ trasto bhaye magno vasāmy udbhrāntacetanaḥ vālinā nikṛto bhrātrā kṛtavairaś ca rāghava
english: Thus I dwell in fear, immersed in dread, my mind distracted, wronged by my brother Vālin, with enmity made between us, O scion of the Raghu clan.

sanskrit: vālino me bhayārtasya sarvalokābhayaṃkara mamāpi tvam anāthasya prasādaṃ kartum arhasi
english: O you who dispel the fear of all the worlds — I, tormented by fear of Vālin, masterless as I am, you ought to show grace to me as well."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu tejasvī dharmajño dharmavatsalaḥ pratyuvāca sa kākutsthaḥ sugrīvaṃ prahasann iva
english: Thus addressed, that splendid one, the knower of dharma, the lover of dharma — that Kākutstha replied to Sugrīva almost with a smile:

sanskrit: upakāraphalaṃ mitram apakāro 'rilakṣaṇam adyaiva taṃ haniṣyāmi tava bhāryāpahāriṇam
english: "A friend is one whose fruit is helpfulness; harm is the mark of an enemy. This very day I shall slay him who has stolen your wife.

sanskrit: ime hi me mahāvegāḥ patriṇas tigmatejasaḥ kārtikeyavanodbhūtāḥ śarā hemavibhūṣitāḥ
english: For these arrows of mine are swift as wind, feathered, of sharp brilliance, golden-adorned, born of the groves sacred to Kārttikeya.

sanskrit: kaṅkapatrapraticchannā mahendrāśanisaṃnibhāḥ suparvāṇaḥ sutīkṣṇāgrā saroṣā bhujagā iva
english: Covered with heron feathers, resembling the thunderbolt of Mahendra, well-jointed, with very sharp tips, they are like angry serpents.

sanskrit: bhrātṛsaṃjñam amitraṃ te vālinaṃ kṛtakilbiṣam śarair vinihataṃ paśya vikīrṇam iva parvatam
english: See your enemy who bears the name of brother — Vālin who has committed this offense — struck down by my arrows, like a mountain shattered."

sanskrit: rāghavasya vacaḥ śrutvā sugrīvo vāhinīpatiḥ praharṣam atulaṃ lebhe sādhu sādhv iti cābravīt
english: Hearing the words of the scion of the Raghu clan, Sugrīva, lord of the host, was filled with incomparable joy and cried out "Well said! Well said!"

sanskrit: rāmaśokābhibhūto 'haṃ śokārtānāṃ bhavān gatiḥ vayasya iti kṛtvā hi tvayy ahaṃ paridevaye
english: "I, overwhelmed by grief just as Rāma is, pour out my lament to you — for you are the refuge of those afflicted by grief — counting you as my companion.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi pāṇipradānena vayasyo so 'gnisākṣikaḥ kṛtaḥ prāṇair bahumataḥ satyenāpi śapāmy aham
english: For you are the friend made by the joining of hands, witnessed by fire — held dear as life itself — I swear by truth itself.

sanskrit: vayasya iti kṛtvā ca visrabdhaṃ pravadāmy aham duḥkham antargataṃ yan me mano dahati nityaśaḥ
english: And so, counting you as my companion, I speak freely — the grief that lies within, that ever burns my heart.

sanskrit: etāvad uktvā vacanaṃ bāṣpadūṣitalocanaḥ bāṣpopahatayā vācā noccaiḥ śaknoti bhāṣitum
english: Having spoken these many words, his eyes clouded with tears, his voice stricken by weeping, he could no longer speak loudly.

sanskrit: bāṣpavegaṃ tu sahasā nadīvegam ivāgatam dhārayām āsa dhairyeṇa sugrīvo rāmasaṃnidhau
english: But Sugrīva restrained by his fortitude, in the presence of Rāma, that sudden surge of tears which had come upon him like the current of a river.

sanskrit: saṃnigṛhya tu taṃ bāṣpaṃ pramṛjya nayane śubhe viniḥśvasya ca tejasvī rāghavaṃ punar abravīt
english: Having suppressed those tears, having wiped his beautiful eyes and drawn a deep breath, that splendid one again addressed the scion of the Raghu clan:

sanskrit: purāhaṃ valinā rāma rājyāt svād avaropitaḥ paruṣāṇi ca saṃśrāvya nirdhūto 'smi balīyasā
english: "Long ago, O Rāma, I was deposed from my own kingdom by Vālin — having caused me to hear harsh words, the mighty one cast me out.

sanskrit: hṛtā bhāryā ca me tena prāṇebhyo 'pi garīyasī suhṛdaś ca madīyā ye saṃyatā bandhaneṣu te
english: My wife was stolen by him — she who is dearer to me than life itself — and those who were my friends were bound in imprisonment by him.

sanskrit: yatnavāṃś ca suduṣṭātmā mad vināśāya rāghava bahuśas tat prayuktāś ca vānarā nihatā mayā
english: And that most corrupt soul made repeated efforts for my destruction, O scion of the Raghu clan, and the many monkeys sent by him I have slain.

sanskrit: śaṅkayā tv etayā cāhaṃ dṛṣṭvā tvām api rāghava nopasarpāmy ahaṃ bhīto bhaye sarve hi bibhyati
english: Yet out of this same suspicion, even upon seeing you, O scion of the Raghu clan, I did not approach — I was afraid, for all fear when there is reason to fear.

sanskrit: kevalaṃ hi sahāyā me hanumat pramukhās tv ime ato 'haṃ dhārayāmy adya prāṇān kṛcchra gato 'pi san
english: For these alone are my allies, Hanūmān foremost among them — it is because of them that I maintain my life even now, fallen into such hardship as I have.

sanskrit: ete hi kapayaḥ snigdhā māṃ rakṣanti samantataḥ saha gacchanti gantavye nityaṃ tiṣṭhanti ca sthite
english: These affectionate monkeys protect me on all sides — they go with me when I go, and they always remain with me when I remain still.

sanskrit: saṃkṣepas tv eṣa me rāma kim uktvā vistaraṃ hi te sa me jyeṣṭho ripur bhrātā vālī viśrutapauruṣaḥ
english: In brief, this is my situation, O Rāma — why should I say more at length to you? That brother of mine, Vālin of celebrated prowess, is my elder and my enemy.

sanskrit: tadvināśād dhi me duḥkhaṃ pranaṣṭaṃ syād anantaram sukhaṃ me jīvitaṃ caiva tadvināśanibandhanam
english: By his destruction my misery would immediately vanish; my happiness and my very life are bound up in his destruction.

sanskrit: eṣa me rāma śokāntaḥ śokārtena niveditaḥ duḥkhito 'duḥkhito vāpi sakhyur nityaṃ sakhā gatiḥ
english: This, O Rāma, is the end of my grief as reported by one afflicted by grief — whether in sorrow or not, a friend is ever the refuge of a friend.

sanskrit: śrutvaitac ca vaco rāmaḥ sugrīvam idam abravīt kiṃnimittam abhūd vairaṃ śrotum icchāmi tattvataḥ
english: Hearing this speech, Rāma spoke to Sugrīva: "What was the cause from which the enmity arose? I wish to hear it truly and in detail.

sanskrit: sukhaṃ hi kāraṇaṃ śrutvā vairasya tava vānara ānantaryaṃ vidhāsyāmi saṃpradhārya balābalam
english: For having heard the reason for your enmity easily, O monkey, I shall arrange for what follows, having weighed the relative strength and weakness.

sanskrit: balavān hi mamāmarṣaḥ śrutvā tvām avamānitam vardhate hṛdayotkampī prāvṛḍvega ivāmbhasaḥ
english: For my indignation upon hearing of your humiliation is powerful and grows, making my heart throb — like the rushing surge of water in the rainy season.

sanskrit: hṛṣṭaḥ kathaya visrabdho yāvad āropyate dhanuḥ sṛṣṭaś ca hi mayā bāṇo nirastaś ca ripus tava
english: Tell me gladly and with confidence — before the bow is strung, my arrow loosed, and your enemy dispatched."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu sugrīvaḥ kākutsthena mahātmanā praharṣam atulaṃ lebhe caturbhiḥ saha vānaraiḥ
english: Thus addressed by the great-souled Kākutstha, Sugrīva was filled with incomparable delight, together with his four monkey companions.

sanskrit: tataḥ prahṛṣṭavadanaḥ sugrīvo lakṣmaṇāgraje vairasya kāraṇaṃ tattvam ākhyātum upacakrame
english: Then Sugrīva, his face radiant with joy, began to recount to the elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa the true cause of the enmity.

sanskrit: vālī nāma mama bhrātā jyeṣṭhaḥ śatruniṣūdanaḥ pitur bahumato nityaṃ mama cāpi tathā purā
english: "My brother named Vālin, the destroyer of enemies, is my elder — always held in high esteem by our father, and so too by me in former times.

sanskrit: pitary uparate 'smākaṃ jyeṣṭho 'yam iti mantribhiḥ kapīnām īśvaro rājye kṛtaḥ paramasaṃmataḥ
english: When our father passed away, the ministers, saying 'this one is the elder,' installed him, with the highest approbation, as lord of the monkeys over the kingdom.

sanskrit: rājyaṃ praśāsatas tasya pitṛpaitāmahaṃ mahat ahaṃ sarveṣu kāleṣu praṇataḥ preṣyavat sthitaḥ
english: While he ruled over that great ancestral kingdom, I remained always bowing to him in humility, standing like a servant.

sanskrit: māyāvī nāma tejasvī pūrvajo dundubheḥ sutaḥ tena tasya mahad vairaṃ strīkṛtaṃ viśrutaṃ purā
english: There was a powerful demon named Māyāvī, the firstborn son of Dundubhi — between him and Vālin there arose a great enmity, over a woman, as is well known of old.

sanskrit: sa tu supte jane rātrau kiṣkindhād vāram āgataḥ nardati sma susaṃrabdho vālinaṃ cāhvayad raṇe
english: He came to the gate of Kiṣkindhā at night while the people slept, roaring with great fury, challenging Vālin to battle.

sanskrit: prasuptas tu mama bhrātā narditaṃ bhairavasvanam śrutvā na mamṛṣe vālī niṣpapāta javāt tadā
english: My brother Vālin, asleep, heard that terrifying roar and could not endure it — he leapt forth instantly.

sanskrit: sa tu vai niḥsṛtaḥ krodhāt taṃ hantum asurottamam vāryamāṇas tataḥ strībhir mayā ca praṇatātmanā
english: Going out in wrath to slay that greatest of demons, he was restrained by the women of the household and by me, who bowed humbly before him.

sanskrit: sa tu nirdhūya sarvānno nirjagāma mahābalaḥ tato 'ham api sauhārdān niḥsṛto vālinā saha
english: But he, the mighty one, shaking off all of us, went out. Then I too, out of brotherly affection, went forth together with Vālin.

sanskrit: sa tu me bhrātaraṃ dṛṣṭvā māṃ ca dūrād avasthitam asuro jātasaṃtrāsaḥ pradudrāva tadā bhṛśam
english: But that demon, on seeing my brother and seeing me standing at a distance, was seized with terror and fled with great speed.

sanskrit: tasmin dravati saṃtraste hy āvāṃ drutataraṃ gatau prakāśo 'pi kṛto mārgaś candreṇodgacchatā tadā
english: As he fled in terror, the two of us pursued him at even greater speed — and the rising moon made the path bright at that time.

sanskrit: sa tṛṇair āvṛtaṃ durgaṃ dharaṇyā vivaraṃ mahat praviveśāsuro vegād āvām āsādya viṣṭhitau
english: That demon, with great speed, entered a large difficult cave in the earth covered over with grass, while we two stood there having reached the place.

sanskrit: taṃ praviṣṭaṃ ripuṃ dṛṣṭvā bilaṃ roṣavaśaṃ gataḥ mām uvāca tadā vālī vacanaṃ kṣubhitendriyaḥ
english: Seeing the enemy enter the cave, Vālin, overcome with anger, his senses agitated, spoke these words to me:

sanskrit: iha tvaṃ tiṣṭha sugrīva biladvāri samāhitaḥ yāvad atra praviśyāhaṃ nihanmi samare ripum
english: "Wait here, Sugrīva, at the mouth of the cave, attentive — until I enter within and slay the enemy in combat."

sanskrit: mayā tv etad vacaḥ śrutvā yācitaḥ sa paraṃtapa śāpayitvā ca māṃ padbhyāṃ praviveśa bilaṃ tadā
english: Having heard these words, I besought him, O scorcher of foes — but he made me swear by his feet, and then entered the cave.

sanskrit: tasya praviṣṭasya bilaṃ sāgraḥ saṃvatsaro gataḥ sthitasya ca mama dvāri sa kālo vyatyavartata
english: More than a full year passed after his entering the cave — and that time elapsed while I stood at the entrance.

sanskrit: ahaṃ tu naṣṭaṃ taṃ jñātvā snehād āgatasaṃbhramaḥ bhrātaraṃ na hi paśyāmi pāpaśaṅki ca me manaḥ
english: I, considering him lost and filled with the agitation that comes from affection — for I could not see my brother — and my mind suspected something terrible.

sanskrit: atha dīrghasya kālasya bilāt tasmād viniḥsṛtam saphenaṃ rudhiraṃ raktam ahaṃ dṛṣṭvā suduḥkhitaḥ
english: Then, after that long time, seeing blood — red and foaming — flowing out from that cave, I was overcome with deep sorrow.

sanskrit: nardatām asurāṇāṃ ca dhvanir me śrotram āgataḥ nirastasya ca saṃgrāme krośato niḥsvano guroḥ
english: And the sound of demons roaring reached my ears, and the outcry of my elder being overwhelmed in battle and crying out.

sanskrit: ahaṃ tv avagato buddhyā cihnais tair bhrātaraṃ hatam pidhāya ca biladvāraṃ śilayā girimātrayā śokārtaś codakaṃ kṛtvā kiṣkindhām āgataḥ sakhe
english: Concluding by those signs that my brother had been slain, and blocking the mouth of the cave with a rock as large as a mountain, I performed the water-rites in grief and returned to Kiṣkindhā, O friend.

sanskrit: gūhamānasya me tattvaṃ yatnato mantribhiḥ śrutam tato 'haṃ taiḥ samāgamya sametair abhiṣecitaḥ
english: The truth I was concealing was diligently ascertained by the ministers — and then, meeting together with them all assembled, I was consecrated as king.

sanskrit: rājyaṃ praśāsatas tasya nyāyato mama rāghava ājagāma ripuṃ hatvā vālī tam asurottamam
english: While I was ruling the kingdom rightfully, O scion of the Raghu clan, Vālin returned, having slain that greatest of demons.

sanskrit: abhiṣiktaṃ tu māṃ dṛṣṭvā krodhāt saṃraktalocanaḥ madīyān mantriṇo baddhvā paruṣaṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Seeing me consecrated, his eyes reddened with anger, he bound my ministers and spoke harsh words to me.

sanskrit: nigrahe 'pi samarthasya taṃ pāpaṃ prati rāghava na prāvartata me buddhir bhrātṛgauravayantritā
english: Though capable of restraining him, against that wicked one, O scion of the Raghu clan, my mind did not stir to action — constrained by reverence for my brother.

sanskrit: mānayaṃs taṃ mahātmānaṃ yathāvac cābhyavādayam uktāś ca nāśiṣas tena saṃtuṣṭenāntarātmanā
english: Honoring that great-souled one duly, I greeted him with proper salutation — and blessings were spoken by him, his inner self apparently satisfied."
